programme: RFX5, the core DNA-binding subunit of the MHC class II enhanceosome (its targets are almost entirely CIITA and the HLA-D antigen-presentation genes plus HLA-E/F), sets up chronic antigen presentation. RORC (RORγt) then commits primed lymphocytes to a canonical Th17 effector programme (IL17A, IL17F, IL22, IL23R, IL21, CCR6, FOXP3, IL2, IFNG, IL6, TNF). BACH2 acts as the brake on that commitment through its known antagonism of PRDM1/Blimp1-driven terminal effector differentiation. Together the three describe an antigen-presentation-to-Th17-effector circuit with its own built-in restraint, not three unrelated factors.
role_in_a: In ccRCC this circuit maps onto the tumor immune microenvironment: MHC-II expression by tumor and stromal antigen-presenting cells (RFX5/CIITA-driven) and Th17/IL-17-producing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (RORC-driven) are recognized features of RCC's heavy immune infiltrate that track with prognosis and checkpoint-immunotherapy response, with BACH2 governing how readily infiltrating lymphocytes convert to that effector state.
role_in_b: In psoriasis this is the disease's principal pathogenic axis: RORC(RORγt)+ Th17 cells producing IL-17A/F and IL-22 drive keratinocyte hyperproliferation and are the direct target of approved biologics (anti-IL-17, anti-IL-23), primed and re-stimulated by RFX5/MHC-II-dependent antigen presentation in dermal dendritic cells and keratinocytes, with BACH2 setting the threshold for that effector commitment.
shared_axis: Both tissues run the same antigen-presentation-primed Th17 circuit — psoriasis as its primary autoimmune manifestation in skin, ccRCC as a heavily immune-infiltrated tumor where the same MHC-II/RORC/BACH2 circuitry operates among tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes; clinically this is the same axis implicated when cancer immunotherapies precipitate psoriasiform flares by releasing Th17 responses.
reasoning: RFX5's target set is essentially the MHC-II enhanceosome and RORC's targets are the textbook Th17 gene signature, so each is individually a recognizable, well-characterized module rather than an artifact of this network, and BACH2 completes them mechanistically via its established PRDM1 antagonism. But no Open Targets association is recorded for any of the three in either disease, and the reader's notes flag that retrieved papers could not be confidently tied to ccRCC or psoriasis, so the account leans on general immunology rather than on anything actually retrieved for this pair.
support: none found — no PMIDs were supplied with the material for RFX5, RORC, or BACH2. ReMap shows RFX5 bound at 9/17 and BACH2 at 3/7 of their listed targets, which supports the genomic reality of those edges but is not disease-specific literature evidence.
how_to_falsify: In matched psoriatic skin and ccRCC tumor-infiltrating-lymphocyte samples, block RORC (e.g. a RORγt inverse agonist) and measure IL-17A/IL-22 output alongside RFX5-target MHC-II expression; if Th17 output in ccRCC TILs does not track with RORC activity, MHC-II expression does not correlate with Th17 infiltration in either tissue, or BACH2 loss fails to raise RORC-target expression, the shared-circuit account fails.
caveats: Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 120 patient-group comparisons, so replication is thinner than the raw fraction implies. RFX5, RORC and BACH2 sit mid-pack (52/120, 52/120, 47/120), well below FOXD2 (76/120) and HOXB5 (70/120); those two were excluded from the account because their target sets (adrenergic/PKA signalling; angiogenesis/RTK signalling) don't form a nameable immune module, not because they recur less often. No Open Targets association is recorded for any of the three carrying factors in either disease, and no tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair.
